inputs.share_count_basis: ADS-equivalent (1 ADS = 2 Class A ordinary shares), so per-share values are per ADS and comparable to the Nasdaq quote. 2,688m ordinary shares outstanding at 30 Jun 2026 (Q2-2026 balance sheet caption) plus ~37m treasury-method dilution from share awards (Q2-2026 diluted weighted average 2,816m less basic 2,692m less ~87.5m if-converted shares of the 2029 convertible notes) = ~2,725m ordinary = 1,362.5m ADS. The US$2.0bn 0.25% convertible (conversion ~US$45.70/ADS, out of the money, holder put June 2027) is carried as DEBT inside total_debt, so its if-converted shares are excluded: counting both would charge it twice. Held FLAT because SBC is fully expensed in the flows.
inputs.net_cash_note: 30 Jun 2026: cash and equivalents 89,068 + short-term investments 132,594 = 221,662. Restricted cash of 13,396 is EXCLUDED (the company's own RMB235.1bn headline includes it). Total debt = short-term debts 3,534 + unsecured senior notes 13,555 current and 16,607 non-current + long-term debts 36,196 = 69,892. Operating lease liabilities (35,416) excluded, see lease_treatment. Caveat: the cash pile is substantially supplier float (accounts payable 228,961 against inventories 114,577), so it is not all distributable if the 1P business shrank; the bear scenario's negative working-capital capture is where that risk is charged.
inputs.reported_fcf_note: FY2025 core_metrics basis: operating cash flow 18,991 less total capex 12,735 (incl. development properties, net of sale proceeds). The company's own FCF definition (also adjusting for consumer-financing receivables) is 6,476 for FY2025 and 31,415 for the twelve months to 30 Jun 2026; FY2025 is a trough year distorted by the JD Food Delivery launch.
inputs.sbc_source: FY2025 share-based compensation 4,726 (core_metrics / non-GAAP reconciliation add-back; H1-2026 1,979 per JD_Quarterly_Q2-2026.txt:865). Cash taxes on net-share settlement are not separately disclosed, so the reconciliation figure is used alone. Interest income 9,056 from JD_Annual_FY2025.txt:14263, stripped because net cash is many times the FCF base.
inputs.buyback_note: FY2025 repurchases RMB21,430m (JD_Annual_FY2025.txt:11868), ~6.3% of shares; H1-2026 a further US$1.0bn (~2.5% of shares), US$1.0bn remaining under the US$5.0bn programme to August 2027. JD is a funded repurchaser: buybacks run at several times SBC, so the flat count is conservative. Repurchases after 30 Jun 2026 are not reflected in either the cash or the share count.
inputs.fx_note: Model in CNY millions, converted CNY->USD at 1/6.6712 = 0.14990 (Yahoo CNY=X, 2026-11-15T03:30Z). Per-ADS basis: 1 ADS = 2 Class A ordinary shares. Parity check against the Hong Kong listing: 9618.HK HK$107.0 per share (2026-11-13 close) x 2 / 7.8455 (Yahoo HKD=X) = US$27.28 per ADS against the Nasdaq close, a ~2.3% gap consistent with the 13-hour difference between the two closes; this confirms the ADS ratio and the FX direction. The Q2-2026 release translated at 6.7851, so the RMB has strengthened ~1.7% since the balance-sheet date. refresh_price does not update fx_rate; re-fetch it with the price.
inputs.wacc_rationale: 9.0% built in CNY, the currency of the flows: China 10-year government bond ~1.8-2.0% plus a ~7% equity risk premium for a China large-cap consumer name at beta ~1.0 gives a cost of equity near 9%; the group is net cash, so WACC ~ cost of equity. Below the 10.5% USD house default by roughly the CNY-USD risk-free differential. The same WACC is used in all three scenarios: VIE, regulatory and subsidy-war risk is charged once, in the flows and in a 25% bear weight, not as a WACC premium.
inputs.lease_treatment: US GAAP (ASC 842) operating leases: the full lease cost is already an operating expense inside non-GAAP EBITDA and operating cash flow, so the flows carry it and operating lease liabilities (35,416 at 30 Jun 2026) are EXCLUDED from net debt. Equivalent to treatment (B); lease_cost_pct_path is therefore zero.
inputs.nci_treatment: Flows are 100% consolidated (JD Logistics ~63% owned, JD Health ~67%, JD Industrials, JD Property). Non-controlling interests are deducted ONCE, in the equity bridge, at book 63,257 (30 Jun 2026). Cross-check at market for the three listed subsidiaries on 2026-11-13 prices (2618.HK 10.27, 6618.HK 40.66, 7618.HK 12.89) with approximate share counts and minority percentages gives ~RMB64bn, in line with book; the share counts used in that cross-check are approximate and it does not cover unlisted minorities (JD Property), so book may modestly understate the claim.
inputs.notes: Model: owner-FCF DCF, component build, 10-year horizon (margins are still recovering from the FY2025 food-delivery trough, so a 5-year build would capitalise an immature margin). Routed as a non-US operating company: owner-fcf.md plus the adaptations (CNY flows / USD quote, NCI, non-operating assets, leases). First valuation of this ticker. FY0 is FY2025; year 1 is FY2026, of which H1 is reported (revenue +0.7% YoY, non-GAAP EBITDA 15,951). No Q3-2026 release was in the folder at the valuation date; it is due imminently and will move year-1 drivers. EBITDA driver is the company's non-GAAP EBITDA (before SBC, excludes interest income, equity-investee results and investment gains), so those assets go into the bridge under the matching-asset rule. CECONOMY (MediaMarkt/Saturn): the takeover completed 2026-11-12, after the balance-sheet date. It is held at cost and kept OUT of the flows: ~EUR1.3bn paid for 59.8% is shown as a cash deduction and an equal asset in the bridge (net zero). CECONOMY's ~EUR23bn of thin-margin revenue will be consolidated from Q4-2026 and is not in base_revenue or the growth path; revisit once JD reports a consolidated quarter. Working capital: JD runs negative working capital (payables + customer advances exceed inventory + receivables by ~9% of revenue), so growth releases cash; captured at 5% of the revenue change in base, and it reverses when revenue falls. Cash tax: profitable entities pay tax while New Businesses losses do not shield it (FY2025 cash tax 8,697), so the rate on consolidated EBIT starts at 45% and ramps to a 20% mature rate (25% statutory, 15% high-tech entities). Price is a regular-session close. The 30% China markdown is applied screener-side, not in this model.

historical_growth.growth_rate_source: judgment: between equity_3yr_cagr (2.4) and revenue_3yr_cagr (7.8), cut for the H1-2026 revenue stall (+0.7% YoY; Q2 -2.9% on the trade-in subsidy comp)
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity CAGR (2.4% 3yr, 7.5% 5yr; total equity including NCI) diverges by more than 30% from revenue (7.8% / 11.9%) and EPS (26.2% / -16.4%): equity is being returned through buybacks and dividends (~10% of market value in FY2025) and EPS endpoints are distorted by the FY2020 investment gains and the FY2025 food-delivery losses. None of the three is a clean growth anchor.
historical_growth.notes: Owner FCF (reported FCF - SBC - interest income): FY2020 27,965; FY2021 10,388; FY2022 22,549; FY2023 26,763; FY2024 31,520; FY2025 -7,526. The FY2025 endpoint is negative, so owner-FCF CAGRs are not meaningful and are left null; FY2020-FY2024 owner FCF compounded at ~3%. Interest income has grown from 2,753 to 9,056 over the period, so an increasing share of reported FCF is yield on the cash pile rather than operating cash. SBC is small (0.36% of revenue) and falling.

base.rationale: Non-GAAP EBITDA margin was 3.9% in FY2023, 4.5% in FY2024 and 1.4% in FY2025; H1-2026 was 2.4%. Year 1 at 2.2% assumes H2-2026 EBITDA of ~13bn against 1.6bn in H2-2025 as food-delivery losses narrow. The mature 3.8% sits below the FY2024 peak, which had trade-in subsidy help and no food-delivery drag. Capex 1.0-1.4% of revenue in FY2024-TTM including development properties net of recycling; D&A 0.74%.

scenario_narratives.base: The food-delivery subsidy war de-escalates into an infrastructure contest and New Businesses losses shrink from roughly RMB40bn a year toward RMB10-15bn by 2029 without ever earning much. JD Retail holds its ~4.5% operating margin as marketplace and advertising revenue outgrow low-margin 1P electronics, and JD Logistics keeps growing external revenue at a mid-single-digit margin. Revenue is flat in FY2026 against the trade-in subsidy comp, then grows 4-5% before fading to 2.5%. Group non-GAAP EBITDA margin recovers to 3.8%, short of the FY2024 peak of 4.5%. CECONOMY is worth what was paid for it and no more.
scenario_narratives.bull: Food delivery reaches breakeven by 2028 and the traffic it brings lifts purchase frequency in core retail; advertising and marketplace take-rate push JD Retail margin above 5.5%; JD Logistics and JD Industrials compound external revenue at double digits. Group EBITDA margin passes the FY2024 peak and settles at 4.8%, with revenue growing 6-7% through 2029. Europe (Joybuy plus MediaMarkt/Saturn) is an option not valued here.
scenario_narratives.bear: Meituan and Alibaba keep the subsidy war going and JD stays a sub-scale number three that cannot exit without writing off the investment; trade-in subsidies are withdrawn and electronics and appliances, 44% of revenue, shrink; PDD and Douyin take share in general merchandise. Revenue barely grows, group EBITDA margin stalls at 2.5%, loss-making units keep the consolidated cash tax rate at 30% because their losses do not shield profitable entities, and a shrinking 1P book starts to unwind the supplier float that funds the cash pile. The terminal multiple is capped at 12x for a structurally challenged retailer. VIE and delisting tail risks are not modelled as flows; they are part of why this scenario carries 25%.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Moved from the 15/50/35 house default. Bear raised to 25%: the thesis depends on an unresolved subsidy war in which JD is a distant third, on a single regulator, and on a VIE structure, and FY2025 showed New Businesses losses can erase most of group profit within a year. Base held at 50%: H1-2026 already shows the margin recovery under way and JD Retail's margin is at a record. Bull cut to 25%: it needs food-delivery breakeven, further retail margin expansion and sustained mid-single-digit growth in a mature market to arrive together.

valuation_philosophy.summary: JD is valued as an operating retailer and logistics group on owner FCF, with the large net cash and investment book added once and the yield on it stripped from the flows. Roughly half of base-case equity value is balance sheet (net cash, investments less minorities) and half is the operating business, so the valuation is less sensitive to the margin path than a typical DCF and more sensitive to whether the cash is real, distributable and reachable through the VIE structure. The market price is close to the balance-sheet value alone, which means it is paying very little for an operating business that earned RMB30bn+ of owner FCF in FY2024; the question the model cannot answer is how much of that discount is the China/VIE discount rather than a view on the flows.
key_risks_to_valuation: Net cash of ~RMB152bn is largely supplier float; it shrinks if 1P volumes fall, and upstreaming it to ADS holders runs through PRC dividend and VIE channels
FY2025 owner FCF was negative; the valuation rests on margin recovery that only H1-2026 has so far evidenced
Consolidated cash tax runs well above statutory while loss-making units persist; a slower ramp to 20% cuts mid-horizon flows materially
CECONOMY is held at cost and outside the flows; integration losses or a write-down are not in any scenario, and neither is upside
NCI deducted at book; listed subsidiaries re-rating upward increases the minority claim on consolidated flows
CNY/USD: every per-ADS value moves one-for-one with the exchange rate, and fx_rate is not refreshed with the price
Q3-2026 results were not available at the valuation date
